title: Plans and recent past
goal: Talk about your plans, what you have (or haven't) done lately, and how long you've been doing something.

grammar.h: ir a + infinitive: the everyday future
grammar.p: To talk about plans, use *ir* (voy, vas, va, vamos, van) + *a* + infinitive. In conversation this is the normal way to talk about the future. Time words like *mañana*, *esta noche*, *el sábado*, *la próxima semana* go at the start or the end.
ex: Voy a llamar a mi mamá esta noche.
I'm going to call my mom tonight.
¿Qué vas a hacer el sábado?
What are you going to do on Saturday?
Mañana va a llover.
It's going to rain tomorrow.

grammar.h: Simple future, and guessing about now
grammar.p: Add *-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án* to the whole infinitive: *viajaré, comerás, vivirá, iremos, estarán*. Common irregular stems: *tendr-* (tener), *podr-* (poder), *saldr-* (salir), *vendr-* (venir), *pondr-* (poner), *har-* (hacer), *dir-* (decir), *sabr-* (saber), *querr-* (querer). It sounds a bit more formal or certain than *ir a*. In everyday speech it is also used to GUESS about the present: *¿Dónde estará?* = I wonder where he is. *Serán las tres.* = It's probably about three.
ex: El próximo año viajaremos a México.
Next year we will travel to Mexico.
Mañana no tendré tiempo.
Tomorrow I won't have time.
Juan no contesta. Estará ocupado.
Juan isn't answering. He's probably busy.

grammar.h: Present perfect: ever, never, yet, lately
grammar.p: *he, has, ha, hemos, han* + participle (*-ar* → *-ado*, *-er/-ir* → *-ido*): *he trabajado, has comido, ha vivido*. Irregular participles: *hecho* (hacer), *dicho* (decir), *visto* (ver), *escrito* (escribir), *puesto* (poner), *vuelto* (volver), *abierto* (abrir), *roto* (romper). Use it with *alguna vez* (ever), *nunca* (never), *ya* (already/yet), *todavía no* (not yet), *últimamente* (lately). For a finished event at a stated time (*ayer, anoche, el lunes*) keep using the preterite. Note: in Mexico you will also hear the preterite with *ya* (*¿Ya comiste?*), which is correct too; in this level's exercises the hint or the options tell you which form is wanted.
ex: ¿Alguna vez has ido a Oaxaca?
Have you ever been to Oaxaca?
Todavía no he hecho la tarea.
I haven't done the homework yet.
Últimamente he dormido mal.
Lately I've been sleeping badly.

grammar.p: Present tense of *acabar* (acabo, acabas, acaba, acabamos, acaban) + *de* + infinitive = to have just done something. Keep *acabar* in the present for this meaning.
ex: Acabo de llegar.
I just arrived.
Mis padres acaban de comer.
My parents just ate.

grammar.h: How long: desde hace, hace … que, llevar
grammar.p: Spanish uses the PRESENT tense for something that started in the past and is still going on. Three common patterns: (1) present + *desde hace* + time; (2) *Hace* + time + *que* + present; (3) *llevar* + time (+ place, or + *-ando/-iendo* form: *trabajando, viviendo, esperando*). To ask: *¿Desde cuándo…?*, *¿Cuánto tiempo hace que…?*, *¿Cuánto tiempo llevas…?*
ex: Vivo en Chicago desde hace diez años.
I've lived in Chicago for ten years.
Hace tres meses que estudio español.
I've been studying Spanish for three months.
Llevo dos horas esperando.
I've been waiting for two hours.
¿Cuánto tiempo llevas en este trabajo?
How long have you been at this job?

vocab: to have been (for a period of time)
to visit (a place) for the first time
to have a birthday, to turn (an age)
phrases: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
What are you going to do this weekend?
A lo mejor voy al cine.
Maybe I'll go to the movies.
Have you ever been to Mexico?
What have you been up to lately?
How long have you been here?
How long have you lived in Chicago?
Hace tres años que trabajo aquí.
I've been working here for three years.
Ha sido una semana muy larga.
It's been a very long week.

items.q: Mañana yo ___ a visitar a mis padres.
items.qen: Tomorrow I'm going to visit my parents.
items.why: A plan for tomorrow → ir a + infinitive. Yo → voy.

items.qen: What are you all going to do on Saturday?
items.why: Ustedes takes the ellos form: van a hacer.

items.q: El próximo año mi esposa y yo ___ a España.
items.qen: Next year my wife and I will travel to Spain.
items.why: 'Mi esposa y yo' = nosotros; future → viajaremos.

items.qen: Tomorrow I won't have time to eat.
items.why: Tener has the irregular future stem tendr- → tendré.

items.q: Your friend is late and not answering. You wonder aloud: 'Where could she be?' Which is natural?
items.why: The simple future expresses a guess about the present: ¿Dónde estará? = I wonder where she is.

items.q: Someone asks you the time. You have no watch. Which reply expresses a guess ('It's probably about three')?
items.why: Future of probability: Serán las tres = it's probably three. 'Son las tres' states it as a fact.
Haber for nosotros in the present perfect is hemos.

items.qen: Have you seen the new movie?
items.why: Ver has the irregular participle visto.

items.qen: I haven't written the report yet.
items.why: Escribir has the irregular participle escrito.

items.q: To a friend: «¿Alguna vez ___ a Oaxaca?»
items.qen: Have you ever been to Oaxaca?
items.why: Tú + present perfect → has ido. 'He ido' is 'I have', 'han ido' is 'they / you all have'.

items.q: How do you say 'I just got home'?
items.why: 'Just did' = acabar in the PRESENT + de + infinitive: Acabo de llegar.

items.qen: I've lived in Chicago for ten years.
items.why: An ongoing situation with the present tense → desde hace + time.

items.q: ___ dos años que trabajo en este hospital.
items.qen: I've been working at this hospital for two years.
items.why: Pattern: Hace + time + que + present.

items.q: How do you say 'I've been in this country for fifteen years'?
opts: Soy quince años en este país.
Llevo quince años en este país.
Llevo en este país desde quince años.
Voy quince años en este país.
items.why: Llevar + time (+ place): Llevo quince años en este país.

items.q: How do you ask a coworker 'How long have you been working here?'
items.why: Still working there → llevar in the present: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas trabajando aquí? 'Trabajaste' means the job is over.
'Lately' → present perfect: he estado (participle of estar = estado).

items.q: A friend asks: «¿Ya has comido?» You haven't eaten yet. Best reply?
opts: Todavía no. Voy a comer en un rato.
Todavía no. Comí en un rato.
items.why: Not yet → Todavía no; the plan to eat soon → voy a comer.

items.q: Mañana mis hijos ___ a las seis.
items.qen: Tomorrow my kids will come at six.
items.why: Mañana → future. Venir has the irregular future stem vendr-; ellos → vendrán.

items.qen: What will you do on your next vacation?
items.why: Hacer has the irregular future stem har-; tú → harás.

items.q: Mi hermano todavía no ha ___ de su viaje.
items.qen: My brother hasn't come back from his trip yet.
items.why: Volver has the irregular participle vuelto.

items.q: Esta noche ___ a cenar con mis amigos.
items.en: Tonight I'm going to have dinner with my friends.
items.why: ir a + infinitive; yo → voy.

items.q: ¿Qué ___ a hacer tú después del trabajo?
items.en: What are you going to do after work?
items.why: Tú → vas a hacer.

items.en: It's going to rain tomorrow.
items.why: Weather uses the él form: va a llover.

items.en: On Saturday we're going to have a party.
items.why: Nosotros → vamos a hacer.

items.q: El año que viene ___ a Guatemala.
items.en: Next year I will travel to Guatemala.
items.why: Infinitive + -é → viajaré.

items.q: Mi hija ___ diez años en mayo.
items.en: My daughter will be ten in May.
items.why: Tener → irregular stem tendr- + á → tendrá.

items.q: Juan no contesta el teléfono. ___ ocupado.
items.en: Juan isn't answering the phone. He's probably busy.
items.why: A guess about the present → simple future: estará.

items.en: —I wonder what time it is. —I don't know, it's probably five.
items.why: Wondering about the present → simple future: ¿Qué hora será?

items.en: Have you eaten yet? (to a friend)
items.why: Tú form of haber → has.

items.en: My parents have never traveled by plane.
items.why: Ellos → han + viajado.

items.en: I haven't done the homework yet.
items.why: Hacer has the irregular participle hecho → he hecho.

items.en: She has never said that.
items.why: Decir has the irregular participle dicho → ha dicho.

items.en: Ma'am, have you ever tried mole poblano?
items.why: Usted → ha + probado.

items.en: Have you all opened the windows yet?
items.why: Abrir has the irregular participle abierto → han abierto.

items.en: Lately my dad hasn't been sleeping well.
items.why: Últimamente → present perfect: ha dormido.

items.en: I just talked with my boss.
items.why: acabar de + infinitive.

items.en: My wife just left.
items.why: 'Just did' keeps acabar in the present: acaba de salir.

items.q: Vivimos en este barrio ___ hace cinco años.
items.en: We've lived in this neighborhood for five years.
items.why: Present + desde hace + time.

items.en: I've been studying Spanish for three months.
items.why: Hace + time + que + present.

items.en: How long have you been waiting, ma'am?
items.why: Usted → lleva + time/gerund.

items.en: Have you ever been to Guatemala? (to a friend)
I haven't finished the report yet.
items.a: Todavía no he terminado el informe.
alt: No he terminado el informe todavía.
No he terminado todavía el informe.

items.en: We have never seen that movie.
I just arrived at the hospital.
My parents just ate.
I've lived in Chicago for ten years.
items.a: Vivo en Chicago desde hace diez años.
alt: Desde hace diez años vivo en Chicago.
Vivo desde hace diez años en Chicago.

items.en: I've been studying Spanish for two years.
items.a: Hace dos años que estudio español.

items.en: How long have you been in the United States, sir?
items.a: ¿Cuánto tiempo lleva en Estados Unidos, señor?
alt: Señor, ¿cuánto tiempo lleva en Estados Unidos?

items.en: It's probably ten at night.
items.a: Serán las diez de la noche.

items.en: I wonder where Ana is at this hour.
Tomorrow I'm not going to have time.
items.a: Mañana no voy a tener tiempo.
alt: No voy a tener tiempo mañana.

items.en: What have you been up to lately? (to a friend)
My sister is going to have a baby in June.
items.a: Mi hermana va a tener un bebé en junio.
alt: En junio mi hermana va a tener un bebé.
Mi hermana en junio va a tener un bebé.

items.say: Voy a llamar a mi hermano mañana.
opts: I'm going to call my brother tomorrow.
My brother is going to call me tomorrow.

items.say: Todavía no he visto a mi médico.
opts: My doctor hasn't seen me yet.
I haven't seen my doctor yet.
I'm going to see my doctor.
They're about to leave for the airport.
They just arrived from the airport.
We just arrived at the airport.
They're going to arrive at the airport.

items.say: Llevo seis meses en este trabajo.
opts: I worked at this job for six months.
I'm going to start this job in six months.
I left this job six months ago.
I've been at this job for six months.
Where is my cell phone going to be?
Where did I leave my cell phone?
I wonder where my cell phone is.

items.say: Hace dos semanas que no duermo bien.
opts: I haven't slept well for two weeks.
I slept well two weeks ago.
I'm going to sleep better in two weeks.
I didn't sleep well two weeks ago.

items.say: ¿Alguna vez ha estado en el hospital?
opts: Were you in the hospital yesterday?
Have you ever been in the hospital?
Are you going to the hospital?
Has he always been at the hospital?

items.say: El sábado vamos a ir a la playa.
opts: On Saturday we went to the beach.
On Saturday we're going to go to the beach.
On Saturdays we go to the beach.
On Saturday they're going to the beach.
My kids came back on Sunday.
My kids come back on Sundays.
My kids want to come back on Sunday.
My kids will come back on Sunday.

turns.es: Oye, ¿qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
turns.en: Hey, what are you going to do this weekend?

opts: Voy a descansar y ver un partido.
Fui a descansar y vi un partido.
Vas a descansar y ver un partido.
turns.why: He asks about plans → ir a + infinitive, yo form: voy a descansar.

turns.es: ¡Qué bien! ¿Ya has ido al nuevo restaurante mexicano de la esquina?
turns.en: Nice! Have you been to the new Mexican restaurant on the corner yet?

opts: Todavía no, pero voy a ir el domingo.
Todavía no, pero fui el domingo.
turns.why: Not yet → todavía no; a future plan → voy a ir. 'Fui el domingo' contradicts 'todavía no'.

turns.es: Te va a encantar. Los tacos son buenísimos.
turns.en: You're going to love it. The tacos are amazing.

turns.es: ¿Dónde estás? Ya son las ocho.
turns.en: Where are you? It's already eight.

opts: Lo siento, saldré de casa ayer.
Lo siento, acabo de salir de casa.
Lo siento, he salido de casa mañana.
turns.why: 'I just left' → acabo de salir. The other two mix tense and time word (future + ayer, perfect + mañana).

turns.es: Bueno. ¿Cuánto vas a tardar?
turns.en: Okay. How long are you going to take?

turns.why: She asks about the future → llegaré en unos veinte minutos. 'Tardé' is past; 'Llevo' means 'I've been (for) twenty minutes'.

turns.es: Está bien. Aquí te espero.
turns.en: Okay. I'll wait for you here.

turns.es: Buenas tardes. Usted es nuevo en el edificio, ¿verdad?
turns.en: Good afternoon. You're new in the building, right?

opts: Sí, llevo aquí desde una semana.
turns.why: Llevar + time + place, present tense: llevo una semana aquí.

turns.es: Bienvenido. Yo vivo aquí desde hace treinta años. ¿Va a vivir aquí mucho tiempo?
turns.en: Welcome. I've lived here for thirty years. Are you going to live here a long time?

opts: Sí, viví aquí por lo menos dos años.
Sí, voy a vivir aquí por lo menos dos años.
Sí, vas a vivir aquí por lo menos dos años.
turns.why: A plan → voy a vivir. 'Viví' is past; 'vas' is the wrong person.

turns.es: Qué bueno. ¿Y ya ha conocido a los otros vecinos?
turns.en: Good. And have you met the other neighbors yet?

opts: Solo he conocido a la señora del segundo piso.
Solo has conocido a la señora del segundo piso.
Solo conoceré a la señora del segundo piso ayer.
turns.why: Answering about yourself → he conocido. 'Has' is tú; 'conoceré … ayer' mixes future with a past time word.

turns.es: Ah, doña Carmen. Es muy amable. Si necesita algo, aquí estoy.
turns.en: Ah, Doña Carmen. She's very kind. If you need anything, I'm here.

items.title: Catching up with an old friend

turns.es: ¡Cuánto tiempo! ¿Qué has hecho últimamente?
turns.en: Long time no see! What have you been up to lately?

opts: Trabajaré mucho y viajaba un poco.
He trabajado mucho y he viajado un poco.
Ha trabajado mucho y ha viajado un poco.
turns.why: She asks with the present perfect about yourself → he trabajado, he viajado. 'Ha' would be he/she.

turns.es: ¿Sabes qué? Mi esposo y yo vamos a tener un bebé.
turns.en: Guess what? My husband and I are going to have a baby.

turns.why: The baby hasn't been born yet → ¿Cuándo va a nacer?

turns.es: En marzo. ¡Estamos muy contentos!
turns.en: In March. We're very happy!

items.title: Small talk at a hospital party

turns.es: ¿Desde cuándo trabajas en el hospital?
turns.en: How long have you been working at the hospital?

opts: Trabajo aquí desde hace un año.
Trabajé aquí desde hace un año.
Trabajo aquí hace desde un año.
turns.why: Still working there → present + desde hace: Trabajo aquí desde hace un año.

turns.es: ¿Y vivías en Chicago antes?
turns.en: And did you live in Chicago before?

opts: No, llevaré un año en Chicago.
No, llevo en Chicago desde un año.
No, llevo un año en Chicago.
turns.why: Llevar (present) + time + place: llevo un año en Chicago.

turns.es: ¡Bienvenido! ¿Ya has probado la pizza de Chicago?
turns.en: Welcome! Have you tried Chicago pizza yet?

opts: Todavía no, pero el sábado he ido a una pizzería.
Todavía no, pero el sábado voy a ir a una pizzería.
Todavía no, pero el sábado fui a una pizzería.
turns.why: Not yet + a plan → voy a ir. The other two say you already went, which contradicts 'todavía no'.

turns.es: ¡Ya me contarás qué tal!
turns.en: Let me know how it is!

turns.es: Papá, ¿por qué no ha llegado el abuelo?
turns.en: Dad, why hasn't Grandpa arrived?

opts: No sé. Estará en el tráfico.
No sé. Estuvo en el tráfico mañana.
No sé. Estarás en el tráfico.
turns.why: A guess about the present → future of probability, él form: estará.

turns.es: ¿Y qué hora es?
turns.en: And what time is it?

opts: No sé, eran como las seis mañana.
No sé, serás como las seis.
No sé, serán como las seis.
turns.why: Guessing the time → serán (plural, agreeing with 'las seis').

turns.es: ¡Ah, mira! Acaba de llegar.
turns.en: Oh, look! He just got here.

roleplay.title: Weekend plans in the break room
roleplay.setup: It's Friday afternoon. You're chatting with Gabriela, a nurse you work with, about plans for the weekend and what you've both been up to lately.
roleplay.persona: You play Gabriela, 34, a nurse originally from Guadalajara, Mexico, who has lived in Chicago for 8 years and has worked at this hospital for 3 years. Friendly, chatty, uses tú. Use short, clear sentences built around this level's grammar: ir a + infinitive, the simple future (including guesses like 'estará cansado'), the present perfect (ya, todavía no, alguna vez, nunca, últimamente), acabar de, and desde hace / hace … que / llevar. Avoid the subjunctive. Facts to reveal only when asked: she just got back from visiting her family in Guadalajara (acaba de regresar); on Sunday she is going to run a 10K race; she has never been to a baseball game at Wrigley Field; lately she has been studying for a nursing certification exam and has slept little. Ask the learner about his plans and whether he has ever been to Guadalajara. If he makes a tense error, react naturally (e.g., '¿Ah, ya fuiste? ¿O vas a ir?') rather than correcting formally.
roleplay.opening: ¡Hola! ¡Por fin es viernes! ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
goals: Tell her at least two things you are going to do this weekend
Find out what she is going to do on Sunday
Ask how long she has lived in Chicago
Ask whether she has ever been to a baseball game
Ask what she has been doing lately

roleplay.title: Meeting an older neighbor
roleplay.setup: You meet Don Ernesto, an older man who lives on your floor, in the elevator. Use usted. Get to know him: how long he has lived there and what his plans are.
roleplay.persona: You play Don Ernesto, 72, a retired baker from Michoacán, Mexico. Polite and warm; use usted with the learner and expect usted back. Speak slowly with simple sentences using this level's grammar: ir a + infinitive, simple future, present perfect, acabar de, desde hace / hace … que / llevar. Avoid the subjunctive. Facts to reveal only when asked: he has lived in the building for 25 years (desde hace veinticinco años); his granddaughter was just born last week (acaba de nacer su nieta); in December he is going to travel to Michoacán by bus because he has never flown on a plane; lately he has been walking every morning in the park. Ask the learner how long he has been in the building and whether he has ever visited Michoacán.
roleplay.opening: Buenas tardes. Usted acaba de llegar al edificio, ¿verdad?
goals: Introduce yourself and say how long you've been living in the building
Ask him how long he has lived there, using usted
Find out his plans for December
Ask whether he has ever traveled by plane
Find out what he has been doing lately
